The five non-placebo cutoffs correspond to distinct legislative phases of the Kulturkampf: \textbf{1872} \emph{Jesuitengesetz} (July 4) expels the Society of Jesus and the \emph{Schulaufsichtsgesetz} (March 11) transfers school inspection to the state; \textbf{1873} the \emph{Maigesetze} (May 11--14) regulate Catholic clerical training, appointment and discipline; \textbf{1874} the Prussian \emph{Zivilehegesetz} (March 9) introduces mandatory state civil marriage in Prussia for the first time; \textbf{1875} the \emph{Personenstandsgesetz} (Feb 6) nationalises civil marriage and birth/death registration alongside the \emph{Brotkorbgesetz} (Apr 22) and the \emph{Klostergesetz} (May 31); \textbf{1876} mass episcopal expulsions leave nine of twelve Prussian bishoprics \emph{sede vacante}. The 1871$^{P}$ column is a pre-Kulturkampf placebo cutoff: a significant coefficient there is a pre-trends signal (see Table~\ref{tab:pretreatment_trends} and \texttt{pretreatment\_trends.tex} for the formal Wald test). $^{*}\,p<0.10$, $^{**}\,p<0.05$, $^{***}\,p<0.01$.
